questions.q: The editorial recalls that motor vehicles created a problem on the roads which led to traffic rules. What does this example show about differences between people?
options: Differences are best avoided by living apart
Not quite. The article says: Differences pose challenges, and challenges stir new thinking and progress.
Differences must be controlled by strict laws
Not quite. The article says: Differences pose challenges, and challenges stir new thinking and progress.
Differences pose challenges, and challenges stir new thinking and progress
Yes. They are to be managed, not removed.
Differences arose only in modern times
Not quite. The article says: Differences pose challenges, and challenges stir new thinking and progress.
questions.rationale: “Differences create challenges. Challenges lead to new thinking. And new thinking results in progress and development… learn the art of ‘difference management’.”

questions.q: How does the article compare Adam’s test in Paradise with our test on earth?
options: The test is the same, but where he had one forbidden tree we live in a whole jungle of them
Right. Whatever makes us forget God and the Hereafter is such a tree.
He had many forbidden trees; we have one
Not quite. The article says: The test is the same, but where he had one forbidden tree we live in a whole jungle of them.
His test was hard; ours is easy
Not quite. The article says: The test is the same, but where he had one forbidden tree we live in a whole jungle of them.
He was tested; we are not
Not quite. The article says: The test is the same, but where he had one forbidden tree we live in a whole jungle of them.
questions.rationale: “In Paradise there was only one forbidden tree, and in this world there is a jungle of ‘forbidden trees’… Only the one who examines his life and continuously introspects will be able to save himself.”

questions.q: What spiritual point does the article make from the recorded message “This number does not exist”?
options: God answers only at certain times
Not quite. The article says: A call addressed to anything other than the one real God goes unanswered.
Technology has made faith harder
Not quite. The article says: A call addressed to anything other than the one real God goes unanswered.
Prayer needs the right form of words
Not quite. The article says: A call addressed to anything other than the one real God goes unanswered.
A call addressed to anything other than the one real God goes unanswered
Yes. The first duty is to discover the real God.
questions.rationale: “If he gives the status of God to a non-god… the answer they receive from all of them, albeit in silent language, is that the number dialed does not exist.”

questions.q: In the article’s reading, what universal law was shown when Moses’ staff became a serpent?
options: The law that miracles belong only to prophets
Not quite. The article says: The law of conversion – that things in nature are constantly changed from one form to another.
The law of conversion – that things in nature are constantly changed from one form to another
Well reasoned. Seed to tree, egg to chick, matter to energy.
The law of gravity
Not quite. The article says: The law of conversion – that things in nature are constantly changed from one form to another.
The law that the strong overcome the weak
Not quite. The article says: The law of conversion – that things in nature are constantly changed from one form to another.
questions.rationale: “Prophet Moses had demonstrated to people a universal and common law of God. This is the law of conversion… Conversion proves intervention, and when intervention is proved, the intervener is also proved.”

questions.q: The Prophet said that those whose hearts are like the hearts of little birds will enter heaven. What quality does the article see in this likeness?
options: A heart free of hatred and revenge – kept so by conscious choice
Exactly. A bird has it by instinct; a person must choose it.
A life free of all cares
Not quite. The article says: A heart free of hatred and revenge – kept so by conscious choice.
A habit of rising early
Not quite. The article says: A heart free of hatred and revenge – kept so by conscious choice.
A love of travel and freedom
Not quite. The article says: A heart free of hatred and revenge – kept so by conscious choice.
questions.rationale: “A heavenly personality is one that is completely free of all negativity. A bird has this positive quality by virtue of its instincts, whereas a heavenly personality has this quality as a conscious choice.”

questions.q: The physicist Satyendra Nath Bose was once given 110 marks out of 100. What lesson does the article draw?
options: Prove yourself able and you receive more than your due – so choose “opportunity activism” over demanding rights
Yes. Be a “giver-member” of society.
Rules should be relaxed for the gifted
Not quite. The article says: Prove yourself able and you receive more than your due – so choose “opportunity activism” over demanding rights.
Rights are won only by protest
Not quite. The article says: Prove yourself able and you receive more than your due – so choose “opportunity activism” over demanding rights.
Examiners often make mistakes
Not quite. The article says: Prove yourself able and you receive more than your due – so choose “opportunity activism” over demanding rights.
questions.rationale: “If a person proves himself competent enough, he will be awarded more than his legal rights… the greatest empowerment is self-empowerment.”

questions.q: The inventor of the AK-47 said he slept well because politicians were to blame. What does the article call this attitude, and what does it set against it?
options: Patriotism, against selfishness
Not quite. The article says: The “blame others” culture of Satan, against the “blame thyself” culture of the angels.
Honesty, against false modesty
Not quite. The article says: The “blame others” culture of Satan, against the “blame thyself” culture of the angels.
The “blame others” culture of Satan, against the “blame thyself” culture of the angels
Correct. A wrongdoer’s proper course is to repent.
Realism, against idealism
Not quite. The article says: The “blame others” culture of Satan, against the “blame thyself” culture of the angels.
questions.rationale: “The ‘blame thyself’ culture is the culture of angels, while the ‘blame others’ culture is the culture of Satan.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, did the Prophet advise his followers not to enter into conflict with rulers?
options: No political system here can be ideal, and endless conflict over it destroys the peace that constructive work needs
Right. Egypt’s sixty years are given as the example.
Religion has nothing to say about justice
Not quite. The article says: No political system here can be ideal, and endless conflict over it destroys the peace that constructive work needs.
Rulers are always in the right
Not quite. The article says: No political system here can be ideal, and endless conflict over it destroys the peace that constructive work needs.
Rulers punish opposition harshly
Not quite. The article says: No political system here can be ideal, and endless conflict over it destroys the peace that constructive work needs.
questions.rationale: “In accordance with the law of nature, no perfect or ideal political system can come into being in this world… practical wisdom demands that people should agree to settle with a less than ideal political system.”

questions.q: In Surah Al-Asr, time is called to witness that man is in loss. Who are named as the exception?
options: Those who believe, do good deeds, and urge one another to truth and steadfastness
Yes. Imam Shafi said this chapter alone would suffice as guidance.
Those who live to a great age
Not quite. The article says: Those who believe, do good deeds, and urge one another to truth and steadfastness.
Those who gather wealth for their children
Not quite. The article says: Those who believe, do good deeds, and urge one another to truth and steadfastness.
Those who withdraw from the world
Not quite. The article says: Those who believe, do good deeds, and urge one another to truth and steadfastness.
questions.rationale: “Man is surely in a state of loss, except for those who believe and do good deeds and exhort one another to hold fast to the Truth, and who exhort one another to steadfastness.”

questions.q: Why does the method of divorce given in the Quran extend over three months?
options: To allow time for dividing property
Not quite. The article says: To leave room for anger to cool and for the couple to reconcile.
To make divorce impossible in practice
Not quite. The article says: To leave room for anger to cool and for the couple to reconcile.
To let the families choose new spouses
Not quite. The article says: To leave room for anger to cool and for the couple to reconcile.
To leave room for anger to cool and for the couple to reconcile
Well read. Three pronouncements in one breath are called a misuse of the law.
questions.rationale: “This method of divorce over a period of three months was devised so that if the husband, in a fit of anger, wants to divorce his wife but later, when his temper cools down, changes his mind… he can do so.”
